name: Edge III
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Loveland Housing Authority built Edge III, the third and final phase of its Edge campus off East 15th Street near Boyd Lake Avenue in east Loveland: 66 studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 60% AMI in three three-story buildings; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $13M of housing authority bonds and opened in early 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows a housing authority finishing a phased campus on land it already owned, issuing its own bonds and combining city fee reimbursements, authority reserves and a CHFA permanent loan to deliver small units for a 4,000-household waitlist.

status.label: Completed and open (grand opening announced for 2026-02-18)
status.detail: Loveland Housing Authority announced a grand opening for 2026-02-18 and its Edge III page says the property is now open and leasing; CHFA's April 2026 eNews congratulated the project on its grand opening. Two of three buildings were at or near completion in June 2025. A placed-in-service date was not found.

next_step: Watch for stabilized occupancy and CHFA's placed-in-service and final credit allocation (8609) figures.

key_numbers.meaning: 24 studios, 30 one-bedroom and 12 two-bedroom units at 30% to 60% AMI (average 49% AMI), bringing The Edge to 205 units.
About $9.2M over 10 years, plus $999,389 of state credit.
Issued by Loveland Housing Authority and privately placed; $8.5M retired at completion, leaving $4.5M permanent, per the application.
Loveland approved fee waivers of up to $1,420,786 on 2023-07-18 under its affordable housing designation.

facts.value: CHFA lists 3735 E 15th Street, Loveland 80538; the application gives Boyd Lake Avenue and 15th Street; the bond notice lists 3705, 3715 and 3725 E 15th Street; the authority's page gives 3875 E 15th St
Three three-story walk-up buildings (about 52,170 sq ft), wood frame on slab, cement board siding with partial stone veneer, TPO flat roofs; Enterprise Green Communities 2020
Studios 469 sq ft; one-bedrooms 605-621 sq ft; two-bedrooms 860 sq ft

Owned by Loveland Housing Authority, fully zoned with off-site improvements complete; the site is next to Edge I and II, removed from the metro district for funding purposes but still bound by its architectural guidelines
The Edge III LLLP (or another authority affiliate), per the bond notice
Aspire, the authority's nonprofit partner, provides resident navigation, health, veteran and transportation support; shared clubhouse, playground and community garden
Edge III accepts Housing Choice Vouchers; the application noted studios suit potential state vouchers for special populations such as homeless youth
Lottery with a preference for people who live or work in Loveland; interest list deadline 2025-10-15

money.note: 2023 Round Two award, matching the application request (the letter of intent asked for $750,000).

Issued by Loveland Housing Authority, privately placed with a lender picked by RFP; all tax-exempt with a small taxable piece of the construction loan; the 2024 bond notice allowed up to $15,000,000 with a TEFRA hearing on 2024-09-16 and approval by Loveland City Council required.

Loveland's Affordable Housing Commission voted on 2023-04-18 to allocate the City of Loveland's private activity bond allocation of $4,641,022 to the housing authority; the minutes do not name the project, so its use for Edge III is inferred.
Approved by City Council on 2023-07-18; the city's fee estimate totals $1,420,785.10 across the three buildings; the city also forgives construction sales and use taxes, per the application.

The application planned a Division of Housing request; the authority's board agenda of 2024-01-24 listed resolution 809 authorizing an application to the Division of Housing's Transformational Housing Loan Fund for Edge III. The award amount was not verified.
Wells Fargo and Loveland Housing Development Corporation are named among funders.

parties.role: Developer and owner (as CHFA prints it)
parties.name: Loveland Housing Authority
Housing Authority of the City of Loveland (Loveland Housing Authority)

background.text: The Edge was built in phases on the old Crystal Rapids water park area by East 15th Street and Boyd Lake Avenue: Phase I (70 units, completed 2016) included homes for High Park Fire and 2013 flood survivors and supportive housing for homeless veterans, and Phase II added 69 units; Phase III completes the 205-unit campus.

The application cited a waitlist of nearly 4,000 households, portfolio vacancy under 2% and a 24% total capture rate, and requested a basis limit waiver because of construction costs and high tap fees.

The application planned groundbreaking in summer 2024 (vertical construction in spring 2024) and completion by summer 2025; groundbreaking happened in December 2024 and the property opened in early 2026.
Pinkard reported in June 2025 that the project was on time and on budget despite spring weather delays, with two of three buildings at or nearing completion.

Letters of support came from the Mayor of Loveland, a Ward IV council member, the city's Community Partnership Office, Disabled Resource Services, the Salvation Army, Aspire 3D and the League of Women Voters, per the application.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's 2023 award report lists $918,458 of federal 4% credit, while CHFA's April 2026 eNews says $933,636.
The project address appears as 3735 E 15th Street in CHFA reports, 3705, 3715 and 3725 E 15th Street in the bond notice, and 3875 E 15th St on the housing authority's Edge III page.
CHFA's award description says Edge III was built with an all-electric design, while the housing authority's Edge III page lists gas heating among unit features.
The housing authority announced a grand opening on 2026-02-18, while CHFA's April 2026 eNews says the grand opening was celebrated that month.
Mile High CRE's groundbreaking article says Phase II was completed in 2021, while its June 2025 article says 2020.

open_questions: Bond closing date, final bond amount and purchaser, equity investor and credit price, and total development cost.
Whether the Division of Housing awarded the requested $2.64M (a larger state award figure appears in search results but could not be verified at a working public link).
City Council approval of the bonds after the 2024 TEFRA hearing, and the city fee reimbursement mechanism.
